text:
- chief complaint: low back pain after lifting a refrigerator about five days ago, with a history of prior discectomy.
- history of present illness: the patient, a 55-year-old male, felt a pain in the lower right back while helping move a refrigerator five days ago. He has been taking ibuprofen, and combined ibuprofen with acetaminophen once for relief. Pain is worse with bending. He is worried about his prior surgery.
- physical examination: vital signs normal, afebrile, blood pressure controlled. Heart regular rate and rhythm; lungs clear. Tenderness to palpation of the right lumbar paraspinal muscles, decreased lumbar flexion and extension, positive right straight leg raise, and good bilateral lower extremity strength. Lumbar spine x-ray shows good alignment without fracture. Labs normal.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right lower back pain; no leg pain, numbness, tingling, bladder or bowel changes, chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting.
- new medications prescribed or changed: meloxicam 15 mg once daily; tramadol (Ultram) 50 mg every 4 hours as needed; ibuprofen discontinued; acetaminophen (Tylenol) may continue.
- follow-up instructions: MRI of the lumbar spine to rule out other causes; physical therapy referral after MRI results; call the doctor for any needs.
